_doc:
T-1232. Every matched resident-research block (asserted_identity: true) read once, by hand, for the person-profile facts it states and the record does not hold. A row is a CANDIDATE FACT and never a finding on its own: tools/spend_person_facts.py adjudicates it, holds the verdicts against its own rules, and writes only the asserted ones onto the records. The file is the reading; the table at data/residents/person_facts.json is what the reading became. Both are gated by `spend_person_facts.py --check`.

WHY SO MANY ROWS ARE WITHHELD. Three standing rulings do most of the withholding and none of them is this ticket's to overturn: T-0513/T-0514/T-0515 say a later-volume reading may date and corroborate and may never promote, so a birth year arithmetic'd out of an 1876 death notice is `later_only`; a source that places the person somewhere else is `outside_chicago`; and a trade, office or interest belongs to the plural-roles field T-1145 is building, so it is `unresolved:T-1145` here rather than spent twice. A withheld fact is not a lost one — it is written down with its reason, which is the whole point of the table.

NO PERSON IS CREATED BY THIS FILE. A marriage names a spouse and a chronology names a travelling companion; neither mints a household member. T-1170 fills families from exactly these rows.

fact_classes.arrival_at_chicago: A dated arrival at Chicago, stated by a source rather than bounded by a postal return.
fact_classes.sex: Stated or titled by the source; never guessed from a forename here (that is T-1168).
fact_classes.name_as_printed: A fuller or different printing of the name, carried BESIDE the read name and never over it.
fact_classes.birth_year_bound: A birth year or bracket, usually arithmetic from an age at death.
fact_classes.death: A dated death, with its place where the source gives one.
fact_classes.marriage: A dated marriage and the party the source names.
fact_classes.life_event: Anything else dated the source states about the person.
fact_classes.departure_from_chicago: A dated leaving, which bears on presence and never moves it.

no_candidate._doc: Matched blocks whose text is the consolidation's own 'Independently corroborated; confirmed, not moved' — a verdict on the identity that proposes no fact about the person. Listed so the table can prove all 94 matched blocks were read, rather than only the ones that yielded.

andrus_thomas.reason: The DuPage history gives a day, and the household's own arrival block is explicit that its 1835-03-31 is a BOUND FROM THE RETURN and not an arrival. The two are different claims about different things and both stand; the bound is not touched.

andrus_thomas.value: Returned east in the autumn of 1834
andrus_thomas.reason: A dated leaving, carried as a life event. It does not move present_on_scene_date, which stays 'uncertain' on its own reasoning.

andrus_thomas.quote: arrival back at Chicago in June 1835
andrus_thomas.reason: The month before the scene date, from the same chronology. Recorded as the source states it and not converted into presence on 1 July.

andrus_thomas.quote: before settling in DuPage in July
andrus_thomas.reason: The same month as the scene. It is why the record's presence is 'uncertain' rather than 'present', and writing it down is what makes that grade legible instead of unexplained.

lampman_henry_s.reason: The compilation says where he was of when the brickyard engaged him. An origin is a fact about the person and does not depend on a Chicago address.

lampman_henry_s.quote: Tyler K. Blodgett's spring 1833 north-side brickyard engaged Henry S. Lampman ... as a workman
lampman_henry_s.reason: A named workplace is a location finding and T-1147 owns the location spend, with its 123 location limits. Recorded here so the lead is not lost; not written as a works_at.

lampman_henry_s.quote: it calls him Chicago's first brickmaker
lampman_henry_s.reason: The record already carries brickmaker as his occupation from this reading.

chandler_joseph.quote: Chandler arrived from Buffalo on 27 June 1833 with Samuel Jackson and Shapley
chandler_joseph.reason: Andreas gives the day. The household's 1834-04-01 is a postal bound and is not touched.
Where he came from, in the same sentence as the day he came.

chandler_joseph.value: Travelled to Chicago with Samuel Jackson and Morgan L. Shapley
chandler_joseph.reason: Two named companions, one of whom (Samuel Jackson) this layer carries. A shared journey is not a household and mints nobody; it is the kind of tie T-1170 will read.

chandler_joseph.value: executive charge of the Chicago harbour work
chandler_joseph.quote: having executive charge of Chicago harbor work that began 1 July 1833
chandler_joseph.reason: A dated office. The plural-roles field T-1145 is building is where a second role belongs; asserting it into the single occupation field here would have to displace one.

jackson_samuel.quote: Samuel Jackson arrived from Buffalo June 27, 1833
jackson_samuel.reason: The same journey Andreas dates for Joseph Chandler, from the other end. Two independent readings of one arrival agree to the day.
Stated in the same sentence as the day he arrived. The household's origin block reads 'Not attested.' and this is the source that attests it.

jackson_samuel.value: foreman of the Chicago harbour construction
jackson_samuel.quote: served as foreman of Chicago harbor construction for some time
jackson_samuel.reason: A trade the record does not hold, and a second role for a person whose occupation field can take one value. T-1145 is the field for it.

hugunin_leonard_c.quote: record Leonard C. Hugunin as arriving 17 August 1833
hugunin_leonard_c.reason: The Old Settlers' proceedings give the day. The household's 1835-06-30 is a postal bound and stands.

hugunin_leonard_c.quote: the 1839 Chicago directory lists Leonard C. Hugunin as a speculator
hugunin_leonard_c.reason: 1839 is four years after the scene. Under the ladder ratified 2026-09-03 (T-0513/T-0514/T-0515) a later volume may date and corroborate and may never promote a trade into 1835.

woodworth_james_h.quote: James Hutchinson Woodworth moved to Chicago in 1833
woodworth_james_h.reason: The household already carries 1833 at year precision. The U.S. House historian's biography is the independent source behind it, and the pass's own ledger calls this a safe chronology enrichment; the row records which source the year rests on rather than adding a second one.
The middle name behind the record's 'James H.'. Carried beside the read name; the card's displayed name does not move.

orsemus_morrison.quote: Orsemus Morrison came to Chicago in 1833
orsemus_morrison.reason: The household already carries 1833 at year precision. The album is the source that says so, and naming it is worth more than repeating the year: the arrival was minted without a citation a query could reach, and this row is that citation.

The record displays 'Morrison Orsemus' — the same two words the other way round. The album prints Orsemus as the forename. The printing is carried; whether the CARD should lead with it is the question T-1217 owns, and this row is not allowed to answer it.
A trade the occupation field reads as none_recorded. T-1145 is replacing that field with dated plural roles and is where this belongs.

cleland_martin.quote: traveled from Chautauqua, New York, to Chicago on a prospecting tour in 1834
cleland_martin.reason: Where he travelled from. An 1886 family genealogy is a late source for a trade or an address and an ordinary one for where a family was of.

cleland_martin.value: A prospecting tour to Chicago in 1834
cleland_martin.quote: to Chicago on a prospecting tour in 1834
cleland_martin.reason: A dated visit, and the thing that puts the postal name in the town at all.

cleland_martin.value: Selected a future home near Niles, Michigan; the family moved west in 1835
cleland_martin.quote: selected a future home near Niles, Michigan; the family moved west in 1835
cleland_martin.reason: The destination is Niles and not Chicago, so nothing here can become a July 1835 Chicago residence. Recorded because it is the reason the presence on this card cannot be lifted.

pugsley_john_k.quote: left near Utica, New York in June 1835
pugsley_john_k.reason: Where he set out from, with the month he set out. The household's origin block reads 'Not attested.' and an 1880 county history is an ordinary source for where a family was of.

pugsley_john_k.value: Travelled to Chicago in June 1835 and prospected there
pugsley_john_k.reason: Dated to the month before the scene, directly adjacent to the 1 July letter-list return the record is minted from.

pugsley_john_k.value: Returned to Paw Paw Township and entered land
pugsley_john_k.quote: then returned to Paw Paw Township and entered land
pugsley_john_k.reason: A transient, not a resident. The record's presence stays where it is and this row says why.

kingston_paul.value: Came from Chicago to Racine on 2 January 1835
kingston_paul.quote: a Racine old-settlers record says he came from Chicago on January 2, 1835
kingston_paul.reason: A dated leaving six months before the scene, and the strongest thing this card holds about where the man was on 1 July. Presence is not moved by this ticket; the fact is written down so the next reader can move it on evidence.

kingston_paul.quote: identify Paul Kingston as a Chicago landholder
kingston_paul.reason: Landholding is a fact about the person that the early-Chicago sources state; it is not a residence and is not read as one.

hobson_jesse.value: Married Catherine Daugherty at Naperville on 6 April 1835
hobson_jesse.quote: married Catherine Daugherty at Naperville on April 6, 1835
hobson_jesse.reason: A dated marriage, the party named, three months before the scene. It names a spouse and MINTS NOBODY: no person record is created and no household membership follows, which is the rule T-1170 will fill families under.

hobson_jesse.quote: Jesse Hobson was living in Cook County in 1835
hobson_jesse.reason: The county and not the town. Recorded at the level the source states it, which is why it cannot lift the card's presence.

mitchell_henry.value: At work in Chicago wagon-factory work in 1834
mitchell_henry.quote: places Henry Mitchell in Chicago wagon-factory work in 1834
mitchell_henry.reason: A dated appearance in the town a year before the postal seed, from an 1883 old-settlers report. Carried as the event it is; the trade itself is T-1145's.

boilvin_nicholas.value: Named in the 1833 Treaty of Chicago payment schedule
boilvin_nicholas.quote: independently in the 1833 Treaty of Chicago payment schedule
boilvin_nicholas.reason: A contemporary federal record naming the person at Chicago, two years before the scene. It is the reading that corroborated the identity and it was carried only as prose.

vasseur_noel.value: Named in the 1833 Treaty of Chicago payment schedule
vasseur_noel.quote: independently in the 1833 Treaty of Chicago payment schedule
vasseur_noel.reason: Contemporary and at Chicago. The block's own warning about later Will and Kankakee geography is the next row and is not softened by this one.

vasseur_noel.value: Later of the Will and Kankakee country
vasseur_noel.quote: later Will/Kankakee geography means the letter must not be converted into a Chicago household claim
vasseur_noel.reason: The block states this as the reason the postal name may not become a household. Written down so the refusal is legible rather than implicit.

lathrop_samuel_s.value: An early member of Chicago's First Baptist Church after its organisation of October 1833
lathrop_samuel_s.quote: names Samuel S. Lathrop as one of the church's early members after its October 1833 organization
lathrop_samuel_s.reason: A dated Chicago appearance nearly two years before the postal seed the record is minted from.

lathrop_samuel_s.value: Built the fence around Rev. A. B. Freeman's Chicago grave
lathrop_samuel_s.quote: records him building the fence around Rev. A. B. Freeman's Chicago grave
lathrop_samuel_s.reason: An undated act in the source, bounded to the church's early years. Carried at year precision with the source's own vagueness intact.

hathaway_joshua.value: Drew the 1834 Chicago cadastral map this project reads as a tier-1 source
hathaway_joshua.quote: the named creator of the 1834 Chicago cadastral map already registered as a tier-1 project source
hathaway_joshua.reason: The map carries his authorship and the project already stands on the map. This is the rare case where the corroborating record is one of the project's own primary sources, so it is graded attested.

elston_daniel.quote: identifies the English merchant who reached Chicago in 1833
elston_daniel.reason: The finding aid says where he was from. The household's origin is null and this fills it with the source that states it.
The household already carries 1833-11-26, a sharper date from the paper's first issue. A year is not an improvement on a day and does not displace it.

elston_daniel.quote: later operated a distillery and brewery
elston_daniel.reason: The finding aid's 'later' is after the scene and undated. A trade the person took up afterwards is not an 1835 trade.

barrows_mary.value: Associate and assistant of Miss Chappel in the town's first school
barrows_mary.quote: name Mary Barrows as Miss Chappel's associate/assistant
barrows_mary.reason: A dated Chicago role stated by the education histories. The teaching trade itself is T-1145's field; the association with a named person is this one.

barrows_mary.value: The LaSalle Street boarding house for scholars
barrows_mary.quote: a participant in the LaSalle Street boarding house for scholars
barrows_mary.reason: A named premises on a named street. T-1147 owns the location spend and its limits; recorded here so the lead survives.

The source titles Chappel and not Barrows. Reading a sex off the forename alone is exactly what T-1168 was written to do under a stated rule, and doing it here without one would be the guess that ticket exists to avoid.

andrews_davi.quote: identifies David Andrews in Cook County from 1834
andrews_davi.reason: The biography prints the forename the postal transcription clipped to 'Davi'. Carried beside the read name — the id and the displayed name do not move, which is the rule the whole layer is minted under.

andrews_davi.quote: in Cook County from 1834 and supports exact-name continuity
andrews_davi.reason: The county, which is what the source says. The block is explicit that it does not reach a 1 July 1835 roof and this row does not either.

clarke_h_b.quote: The 1837 election return prints 'Henry B. Clarke', expanding both initials of H. B. Clarke
clarke_h_b.reason: 1837 is two years after the scene. The expansion is real and is recorded; under T-0513/T-0514/T-0515 a later volume may date and corroborate and may never promote, so the card's name stays H. B. Clarke.

clarke_h_b.value: Dr Henry Clarke, died at Walworth, Wisconsin, before 23 April 1853, aged 60
clarke_h_b.quote: Clarke, Dr. Henry, died, Walworth, Wis., before April 23, 1853, aged 60
clarke_h_b.reason: The pass refused this in terms: surname and first initial only, a doctor rather than a hardware merchant, and a Wisconsin death. A different man. Recorded so the refusal is legible and cannot be re-made as a find.

collins_j_h.quote: The 1837 election return prints 'James H. Collins.', expanding both initials
collins_j_h.reason: The 1837 return is what makes the identity and it is still 1837. The expansion is recorded and not promoted into the 1835 card.

collins_j_h.value: Moved to Illinois in 1833 and practised at Chicago in 1834 with his former student John D. Caton
collins_j_h.quote: says he moved to Illinois in 1833, and records his 1834 Chicago practice with former student John D. Caton
collins_j_h.reason: Dated before the scene, and it names a second person this layer carries. The partnership is a working tie and not a household.

stewart_r.quote: Fergus 1839, 'Stewart, Royal, attorney at law, Lake street', and the 1837 election return, 'Royal Stewart'
stewart_r.reason: Two later records expand the bare R. the same way, which is the discriminator that made the identity. Both are after the scene, so the expansion is recorded and the card's name does not move.

thrall_e_l.quote: The 1837 election return prints 'Edward L. Thrall'
thrall_e_l.reason: 1837, and the ladder's rule about later volumes applies whatever the reading reaches.

thrall_e_l.value: In Chicago and in ward 1 on 2 May 1837
thrall_e_l.quote: carries that he was in Chicago and in ward 1 on 2 May 1837
thrall_e_l.reason: A dated appearance two years after the scene. It corroborates and dates; it does not say anything about 1 July 1835.

sabine_wm.quote: Fergus 1839 prints 'Sabine, William A., boarding-house, 161 Lake street, up stairs'
sabine_wm.reason: The block itself says the middle initial A. is 1839's and is carried as 1839's, not as an 1835 fact. This row is that ruling, written where a query can reach it.

marshall_j_a.quote: Fergus 1839 prints 'Marshall, James A., auctioneer, commission, etc., So. Water st', expanding J. A. exactly
marshall_j_a.reason: An exact expansion, four years late. Recorded, not promoted.

marshall_j_a.value: James Monroe Marshall, real estate, died 1 July 1880, aged 45-9
marshall_j_a.quote: the old-settler notice 'Marshall, James Monroe, real estate, died July 1, 1880, aged 45-9'
marshall_j_a.reason: The pass refused it: a middle name conflicting with the A., and an age that would make him an infant in 1835. Not the same man, and the refusal is kept where it can be seen.

grant_james.value: Died at Oakland, California, 14 March 1891, aged 78
grant_james.quote: Grant, James, lawyer, died, Oakland, Cal., Mar. 14, 1891, aged 78
grant_james.reason: An old-settler death notice. Under the ladder it may date and corroborate and may never promote; the arithmetic it supports is the next row and is withheld on the same rule.

grant_james.quote: The 1891 age puts his birth at 1812-13, which makes him about 22 in the scene
grant_james.reason: The block does the arithmetic and stops. So does this: a birth year arithmetic'd from an age at death in 1891 is a later-volume reading, and T-0513/T-0514/T-0515 hold it out of the 1835 card.

myers_frederick.quote: served as quartermaster's clerk at Fort Dearborn in 1831-33
myers_frederick.reason: A dated Chicago post before the scene, from a 1928 local history that names the fort. The office itself is a role and T-1145's; the dated presence at the fort is the fact carried here.

myers_frederick.value: A veteran of the War of 1812
myers_frederick.quote: identifies Frederick Myers as a War of 1812 veteran
myers_frederick.reason: A biographical fact stated outright. It bears on his age without naming one, and it is not turned into a birth year here.

wright_john_s.value: Bought Chicago land and original-town lots
wright_john_s.quote: identifies John S. Wright's Chicago land purchases and original-town lots
wright_john_s.reason: Landholding, stated by the library's finding aid. The block is explicit that later deed dates are not back-projected, and this row carries no deed date.

wright_john_s.value: Later deeds recorded in the finding aid
wright_john_s.quote: Later deed dates are not back-projected to 1835
wright_john_s.reason: The block's own refusal, made into a row so it can be counted rather than read.

harmon_elijah_d.reason: An obituary line in a volume printed 34 years after the scene. Under the ladder ratified 3 September 2026 (T-0513, applied by T-0514/T-0515) a volume printed after the scene date may date and corroborate and may never promote. The reading is kept; the 1835 card does not move.

harmon_elijah_d.quote: a death date and age that put birth about 1788-89
harmon_elijah_d.reason: The age at death puts the birth about 1788-89. The record already carries a birth of 20 August 1782 at Bennington, graded attested out of Andreas, and the two do not agree. Neither is smoothed into the other: the arithmetic is recorded as the contradiction it is, which is what the card needs in order to be disagreed with.
The 1843 directory prints the full given names, which the record already displays.

heacock_russel_e.quote: one of two American families occupying the old log officers’ quarters inside the pickets of the ungarrisoned fort in July 1827
heacock_russel_e.reason: A dated Chicago residence eight years before the scene, and the earliest thing the corpus holds about this man. It is contemporary in what it describes and it settles nothing about 1 July 1835, which is why it is a life event and not an arrival.

Its obituary list also prints 'Hogan, John Stephen Coates, early postmaster, died, Memphis, Tenn., 1866' — a different place and a different year. Both readings are recorded and neither is asserted; a source that disagrees with itself is evidence about the source.

hogan_john_s_c.quote: Hogan, John Stephen Coates, early postmaster, died, Memphis, Tenn., 1866
hogan_john_s_c.reason: The second of the volume's two death readings for the same man. Recorded beside the first so the disagreement is visible rather than resolved by whichever line was read last.
